name: La Siguanaba
description: La Siguanaba is a shapeshifting female spirit of Central American folklore who appears to lone travellers — typically unfaithful or wayward men — as a beautiful long-haired woman seen from behind, then turns to reveal a horrifying face (a horse skull or a death's head). She lures her victims to ravines or rivers, where they may be driven mad or killed.

aliases.name: Sihuehuet
aliases.meaning: 'beautiful woman' — her original name in Salvadoran Cuscatleca tradition

origin: Central American folklore from southern Mexico to Costa Rica, with regional variants in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Costa Rica.
